meta.audit_type: final-pass re-audit of the exact fixed commit
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md
meta.environment: WSL bcftools 1.24 / htslib 1.24; synthetic archived fixtures

findings.evidence: All archived and fresh inputs completed; no unsafe or scope-violating behavior was observed.

findings.finding: reheader -f changes contig header lines but not record CHROM values; annotate --rename-chrs must be used before merging mismatched contig names.
findings.evidence: fresh contig-records: header-only records remained 1,2; annotate merge produced 361 sites x 8 samples with a tuple hash equal to the joint truth.

findings.finding: The naive-concat recovery now distinguishes a one-file reorder (use plain concat) from a naive path (apply view -s with the same order to every input).
findings.evidence: fresh naive-reorder: both plain concat after a one-file reorder and --naive after normalizing every input produced 361 records and the joint-truth tuple hash.

archived.summary: Validated missing-vs-hom-ref merge behavior, concat/overlap handling, normalized isec, subset tag recomputation, contig/sample harmonization and sorting, SV scope routing, and duplicate sample-name handling.

fresh.summary: Validated the two supported naive-concat recoveries and header-only versus record-level contig repair.

dynamic_results.known_runtime_note: The archived sort case emitted a Windows-mounted-filesystem chmod warning for bcftools temporary storage but still sorted and indexed all 361 records; it is not a skill instruction failure.

scores.score_rationale: The score reflects complete synthetic regression plus targeted fresh execution, clear boundaries, and the P2 correction. It is not independent acceptance evidence and does not claim production-scale or non-synthetic coverage.
